increment_paragraph: **MK-EVENT-DESCRIPTOR-QUANT** (gateway rule 38, contract specification C04.6.2; USER DIRECTION 2026-11-01, "We must decompose the premise into quant like composed clauses."; USER DECISION 2026-11-01, "I approve the changes of D1-D5."): the named premise `mk_event_descriptors` of Monkey's `mk_event_timeout_create`, `mk_event_timeout_destroy`, `mk_event_channel_create` and `mk_event_channel_destroy` is retired and each descriptor effect is a descriptor-cell state: `quant live #data: mk_event.fd |-> #fresh(descriptor) when #result != -1;` (the member names the new descriptor, the result is its witness), `|-> {#stale(descriptor), #kept}` in the failure class, `|-> #stale(descriptor)` at the destroy, `#r_fd: #pointee |-> #fresh(descriptor)` slots with `|-> #same(r_fd)`, and the channel destroy's closes and removal under `when #data: mk_event.fd == #r_fd`; both levels load to one canonical set. The package `rule-38-descriptor-cells` holds the cell table (a release stales every name of an identity; undecided, double, escaping and owner-released cases refuse; the guard is decided only from live identities); `P-CELL-STATE-NOT-FORWARDED` is published with every row resting on a cell-bearing declaration. `QCore.DescriptorCells` (16 theorems). The integrator ran the live-route measurement (`baseline:eb49bb6ce` to `3d3e3db93`, declared): `match` on corpus, slice and system, no status moved. Report: [docs/reports/mk-event-descriptor-quant/README.md](../../reports/mk-event-descriptor-quant/README.md).

ledger.why: Discharged by MK-EVENT-DESCRIPTOR-QUANT: a member-held descriptor identity and a descriptor out slot exist in v1 as descriptor cells (contract specification C04.6.2, gateway rule 38, USER DECISION 2026-11-01 "I approve the changes of D1-D5."); the four declarations are restated with them, their bodies read at 66910c10, 046accf6 and the slice export and pinned at all three; the premise mk_event_descriptors is gone. The declared live-route measurement matched on all three routes (no status moved).

ledger.title: A descriptor cell's object actual whose pointee is a record with struct mk_event as its first member refuses
ledger.text: Registered by MK-EVENT-DESCRIPTOR-QUANT. Rule 38 reads a member cell (`#data: mk_event.fd`) only where every actual of the callee in the calling function is a `struct mk_event *` (Clang's type before the conversion to `void *`), so `ins` (struct flb_input_instance *, flb_input.c input_instance_channel_events_init; flb_output.c flb_output_init_all) and Monkey's `server_timeout` (struct mk_server_timeout *) refuse at the call (`descriptor-cell-undecided`). DISCHARGE: read the first member (C11 6.7.2.1p15: a pointer to a structure, suitably converted, points to its initial member) as the event's cell, with a test that a record whose first member is not the event still refuses, measured.

ledger.title: Array-element descriptor slots (&X->f[K], X->f[K]) never reach rule 38
ledger.text: Registered by MK-EVENT-DESCRIPTOR-QUANT. Rule 38 keys a slot cell `&X->f[K]` and its by-value read `X->f[K]`, but the access gate refuses the array element's member read at a cell-bearing call before rule 38 is asked, so Fluent Bit's channel operations (`&sched->ch_events[0]`, `config->ch_self_events[0]`, ...) keep a gate refusal. DISCHARGE: the gate admits a constant-index element of an integer array member at a withheld declaration's borrowed position (as W44-INDIRECT-CALL-ARGUMENT-ACCESS admits a typed member read), with fixtures, measured.
